question: Clinical audit does not require ethics committee approval because it measures compliance with existing standards rather than generating new knowledge.

l10n.wrongAnswerMessage: Audit is distinguished from research precisely because it measures practice against a known standard rather than generating new knowledge. This distinction is why audit typically does not require ethics committee approval.
l10n.correctAnswerMessage: Correct. Audit is a quality-improvement activity using existing standards and does not generate new knowledge, so it is generally exempt from formal ethics approval, unlike research.
